C0.quote: each voter either delegates to a seemingly attractive proxy or casts a ballot directly
C0.note: Proxy voting / delegation under approval voting; approximation and complexity of proxy selection.

C1.quote: a good approximation of the best possible approval score
C1.note: Most results are approximation bounds on intrinsic approval score (WD); NP-hardness (AL); MovieLens experiments (EM, using synthetic-derived intrinsic preferences).

C2.1.value: preferences / ballots (intrinsic preference profile, revealed preference profile, advertised ballots)

C2.2.quote: approval preferences 𝑣𝑖 ∈ {0, 1}𝑚 over the set of proposals
C2.2.note: Approvals with partial revealed preferences (⊥ for no opinion).

C2.3.quote: we refer those as true or intrinsic preferences

C2.4.quote: voters have intrinsic approval preferences over all proposals
C2.4.note: Separate notation for intrinsic v_i and revealed v̂_i; voters delegate or vote directly with revealed preferences.

C3.1.note: Voters' behaviour is a fixed threshold delegation rule; no voter misreports. dReps are strategic only in an optimisation sense but not modelled as misreporting voters.

C3.2.note: Revealed preferences are partial truthful views of intrinsic ones by definition (v̂_i(j)=v_i(j) or ⊥), but no statement about sincerity of submitted ballots is given as such. Closest: formal relation, not a sincerity statement.

C4.1.note: Inputs are approvals, but utility is not used separately; 'approval score' is the objective. Voter satisfaction mentioned only in abstract; no utility notion in the model.

C4.2.note: Term 'dichotomous preferences' not used by the authors (only in reference title).

C5.1.note: Approximation of the optimal intrinsic approval score (social welfare).

C5.2.quote: how well the intrinsic score of the winning proposal
C5.2.note: Evaluated on intrinsic preferences defined separately from revealed input.

VOT.quote_behav: voter 𝑖 delegates their vote to a dRep when their distance
VOT.note: Voters follow fixed threshold delegation rule; a voter attracted by multiple dReps delegates arbitrarily.

OTH.quote_behav: they can coordinate with each other and advertise their types accordingly
OTH.quote_info: The dReps are fully informed about the preferences of the voters
OTH.note: dReps (proxies) are the other acting agent; they have no preferences, coordinate to maximise the approximation (a fixed designer-like goal). Coded NONSTRAT because they have no objective of their own; info is complete but info set to NA per codebook for NONSTRAT.

C7.1.quote: devoid of personal preferences over the proposals
C7.1.note: Both voters and dReps are non-strategic.
